item.title: Re: Reluctant -1
item.content:encoded:

And if they read We Just Make Toys, and then see the backwards navigation, and go here and read this second, that feels like an alright progression.

The seven lines of space is to — ah shit I just explained this in chat, lemme put it in a collapsible.

3:14 PM <&LearningStuff> The reason that there's blank space at the beginning of my articles? Double purpose:
3:15 PM <&LearningStuff> It acts like a title page, where you can't start reading without scrolling down so you just get the "Vend-a-Friend" logo. Like when a movie opens and there's a sweeping shot with the movie title.
3:15 PM <&LearningStuff> And secondly, the logo isn't transparent, and there's a gradient at the top of the page. If it was any higher, you'd be able to see that it's clearly a rectangular image

item.title: Reluctant -1
item.content:encoded:
This is a weird tale for me because I liked certain parts of it, but other parts felt like they dragged on a bit too long. That, and I feel like it takes away from WJMT by making the reveal of Polly's plagiarism a reveal to Brainy alone.
As an aside, what's with the seven lines of space before the logo/title picture in the new versions of these? I honestly don't see a point to them.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You've made me sympathetic with Polly *and* Brainy.

Granted, I still wouldn't want to be trapped in an elevator with either of them, but sympathetic nonetheless. Little did Polly realize the far-reaching consequences of her pathetic perfidy that day.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Some people were a bit fuzzy on Polly's motives and everything, and felt she didn't have enough screen time, so here she is! In all her glory. Pretty much all to this author post that there is. I liked making this, it was intended to have a part between where it ended and where We Just Make Toys begins, but I found that it worked this way (and had already passed the 3,000 word mark). I shall leave it up to the reader's imagination how exactly it goes down. Yay for a Vend-a-Friend prologue (in case people like it)!
